title: When the Rivergate Burns
premise: When mountain guide Orsen Montrose pulls a seal-stamped chest from the Rivergate's floodwaters, she unknowingly claims proof of a drowned nation's stolen treasury — and a salvage fleet's kill order. Hunted by the corrupt magistrate who sank that nation, Orsen assembles a crew of outcasts: a disgraced cartographer, a river-witch ferrywoman, and the magistrate's own estranged son. Racing six tides to reach the wreck before the fleet, they discover the chest is only one of three keys, and the final key lies in the magistrate's hands. In the burning climax at Rivergate itself, Orsen chooses justice over treasure, exposing the magistrate before the assembled fleet and giving the drowned nation's gold back to its scattered survivors.
about_author: Paloma Sandoval is a former river pilot who spent a decade working the delta towns of two borders, collecting the stories smugglers tell after dark. She writes adventure fiction about people the maps forgot.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Orsen Montrose guides a wealthy client through the high passes above the Rivergate, revealing her blacklisted past and her habit of measuring life in miles. When the client cheats her fee, she walks away into the flood season alone. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: restless isolation, a woman who trusts no one and nothing but terrain.

chapters.title: What the Water Gives Back
chapters.summary: Fishing the flooded shallows for food, Orsen hooks a chest stamped with the seal of Vessany, a nation drowned in a war no one names anymore. Inside: a brass tide-key and a manifest naming a wreck called the Lament. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as she realizes what the seal means.

chapters.title: The Fleet on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Salvage ships appear upriver, flying the magistrate Corvane's colors, dragging chains across every bend. A dying river-runner tells Orsen the fleet seeks 'the Vessany keys' and kills anyone who touches them. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the hunt begins; the chest has made her prey.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Orsen deciphers the manifest: the Lament lies behind the Silt Gates, reachable only during a six-tide window when the river drops. The first tide is tomorrow. She needs a boat, a chart, and luck. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: cold calculation masking fear — the clock is now the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Ferrywoman's Price
chapters.summary: Orsen barges with Maren, a river-witch ferrywoman who demands passage rights to the wreck in exchange for steering her leaky barge through the flooded timber. Their wary alliance forms over cards and threats. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: first crack in her solitude; trust offered like a knife, handle-first.

chapters.title: A Mapmaker's Ghosts
chapters.summary: In the smuggling town of Lowmark, Orsen recruits Tam Vireo, a disgraced cartographer imprisoned for forging Vessany charts — charts he claims were dictated by survivors. He knows where the second key waits. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: guilt and redemption-seeking; a new voice joins the chorus.

chapters.title: Corvane's Son
chapters.summary: The crew is ambushed by a lone rider: Dain Corvane, the magistrate's son, who defects rather than report them, carrying his father's private ledger of the Vessany plunder. Orsen doesn't believe him — yet keeps him alive. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: betrayal of blood for conscience; tension inside the crew.

chapters.title: First Tide Falling
chapters.summary: The barge runs the flooded timber at night while a fleet patrol skiff hunts them by lantern-light. Maren's river-craft saves them; Tam's forged papers buy them through the Lowmark chain. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: the crew becomes a unit under fire.

chapters.title: The Ledger of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Reading Corvane's ledger, the crew learns the truth: the magistrate sank Vessany's refugee ships himself and sold the nation's treasury piecemeal. The Lament holds the last third — and the names of every family he robbed. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: rage hardening into purpose; this is now about justice, not gold.

chapters.title: Second Tide: The Silt Gates
chapters.summary: The gates are guarded by a fleet garrison. Dain talks them open using his father's seal while Orsen and Maren hold their breath below decks. It works — barely — and the garrison commander sends word ahead. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by exposure; the enemy now knows exactly who they are.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Shallows
chapters.summary: A squall forces them into a hidden channel where they find a Vessany survivor village living off the grid. An old woman recognizes the tide-key and gives Orsen a warning: the third key was never lost — Corvane wears it as a signet ring. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: found family echoes; the drowned nation lives in its survivors.

chapters.title: Third Tide: Betrayal at Anchor
chapters.summary: A crew member Tam hired in Lowmark sells their position to the fleet. The patrol burns a fishing camp as a message. Orsen executes the traitor's contract — exile, not death — and the crew's trust fractures. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: the cost of mercy; leadership tested.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: The Lament's Grave
chapters.summary: They find the Lament wedged in a canyon of silt, hull breached but hold intact. Diving in the dropping water, Orsen recovers the second tide-key and the survivor manifests. The fleet's masts appear at the canyon mouth. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: awe and grief among the dead, interrupted by pursuit.

chapters.title: Running the Canyon
chapters.summary: A running gunfight down the narrowing gorge. Maren threads rapids no pilot has survived; Tam takes a graze; Dain turns his father's own signal codes against the pursuers. They escape downstream as the fourth tide closes the canyon behind them. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: exhilaration and bonding — the crew now fights as one body.

chapters.title: Two Keys, One Ring
chapters.summary: Holed up in a sea cave, the crew plans the impossible: the wreck vault needs all three keys, and the third sits on Corvane's hand at the Rivergate citadel. Tam proposes forgery; Dain proposes patricide; Orsen proposes theft. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: strategy as character — each plan reveals its maker.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: Into the Citadel
chapters.summary: Disguised as salvage officers, Orsen and Dain infiltrate the Rivergate citadel during Corvane's victory feast. Orsen lifts the signet from his hand mid-toast; Dain confronts his father face to face and walks away alive. Alarms rise as they flee. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: audacity and heartbreak; Dain mourns the father he never had.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs
chapters.summary: Corvane anticipated the theft — the signet is real, but the citadel gates seal the city. Maren must run the fortified rivergate itself, the one passage no ship survives. The crew votes to try anyway. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve; the point of no return.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide: The Burning Gate
chapters.summary: Under flaming arrows and chain-shot, Maren threads the burning gate as the sixth tide peaks. The barge shatters on the far side; the crew swims ashore with the keys and the manifests, half-drowned, alive. Behind them, the gate burns. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: climax of survival; everything risked, most of it lost.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Falls
chapters.summary: At the Lament's true vault behind the falls, the three keys turn together. Inside: not just gold but Vessany's charter of record — legal proof of Corvane's crimes, sealed for any court that would hear it. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: revelation; the treasure was always the truth.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Corvane's fleet corners them at the falls — but Orsen summons the survivor village and the independent salvagers Corvane has cheated for years. Before the assembled fleet crews, she reads the charter aloud. The fleet turns; Corvane's own captains arrest him. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: catharsis; the law arrives only because people carried it there.

chapters.title: The Weight of Gold
chapters.summary: The treasury is distributed to Vessany's survivors by the old woman's ledger of names. Dain declines his inheritance and asks instead to learn the river. Tam begins drawing new charts — with Vessany restored to them. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: restitution; power returned to the powerless.

chapters.title: Years, After All
chapters.summary: One year later, Orsen guides a small expedition — Maren, Tam, Dain — up the high passes where the story began, no longer measuring life in miles. She plants the Vessany seal at the summit cairn and finally stays to watch the sunset. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: resolution; a woman who counted miles learns to count years, and people.
